output.summary: The ED length-of-stay rise is almost entirely boarding (about 3.0 of 3.2 h). Nurse staffing is flat, with hours per visit, vacancy and grid compliance unchanged. Volume, acuity, staffed beds and occupancy are also flat. Boarding jumped in March, when the hospitalist rounding change took effect. Medical-ward discharges slipped later while surgical wards did not change. A pre-scheduled huddle pilot halved boarding on 4 West, and the other wards served as a control. The early-discharge huddle should be extended. The travel-nurse contract, which would defer case managers, and pausing the huddle would work against the real cause. The effect of the evening bed-cleaning cut is unmeasured, and the link from boarding to front-end delays has a rival explanation in the May triage-provider cut.
